finding_key: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts::the url printed for copy-paste omits `clistate`, so copying it makes the login fail with a misleading "upgrade the server" message
evidence: Verified the full chain in the supplied code: login.ts prints the nonce-less URL (`Opening browser: ${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}`) while oauthUrl carries `cliState`; github-auth.guard.ts:26 returns undefined for an absent cliState so a nonce-less flow is stored; auth.controller.ts redirects with no `state` param when `state.cliState` is falsy; and login.ts's listener then rejects with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE ("Upgrade the server...") and settles the login. A user copy-pasting the visibly printed URL (still documented as a copy-paste affordance in cli.md step 3) thus gets a login failure with a false server-version diagnosis. It is a deliberate secrecy tradeoff with a fallback (the full URL prints when open() throws), and the failure is recoverable by re-running, so impact is a misleading-error UX defect rather than a functional or security break.
